question: What defines an adverse event in healthcare?

options.A: An equipment failure that causes no patient contact
options.B: An unintended injury caused by healthcare management
options.C: The natural progression of a terminal disease process
options.D: A predictable physiological reaction to prescribed medication

explanation: Adverse events specifically stem from medical management or care delivery rather than the underlying disease itself. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h1)

question: How does a near-miss differ from an actual adverse event?

options.A: A near-miss reaches the patient but results in zero harm
options.B: An adverse event only occurs in surgical theatre settings
options.C: An adverse event is always reported while near-misses are ignored
options.D: A near-miss is intentionally planned to test system limits

explanation: Near-misses share the same underlying system vulnerabilities as adverse events, but harm is avoided by timely interception or luck. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h1)

question: What is the very first priority when an adverse event occurs?

options.A: Gathering staff witnesses for formal interrogation
options.B: Completing the mandatory incident report form
options.C: Notifying the hospital legal department instantly
options.D: Immediate stabilization and safety of the patient

explanation: Patient well-being and clinical rescue always come before administrative and investigative duties. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h2)

question: A patient experiences an acute allergic reaction due to a newly administered intravenous drug. What action should be taken right after stabilizing the airway?

options.A: Begin writing the incident report while waiting for the doctor
options.B: Discard the medication bag immediately to clear the workspace
options.C: Preserve the IV cannula, infusion set, and remaining medication vial
options.D: Inform the hospital director before checking vital signs again

explanation: Physical evidence related to the event must be secured to assist in subsequent product or clinical investigations. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h2)

question: How should an adverse event be documented in an incident report?

options.A: Through vague summaries to protect the reputation of the ward
options.B: With speculative assumptions about who caused the equipment failure
options.C: By recording the personal opinions of nursing colleagues nearby
options.D: Using objective, factual descriptions devoid of emotional language

explanation: Incident reports require clear, observable facts rather than speculation or emotional commentary to maintain legal and clinical integrity. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why are institutional incident reports kept separate from the patient's main medical chart?

options.A: To hide mistakes from regulatory bodies and governing councils
options.B: Because clinical charts do not have enough physical paper space
options.C: To ensure doctors never have to read nursing observations
options.D: To protect quality improvement data and internal review processes

explanation: Separating administrative reporting from clinical documentation helps protect internal quality assurance workflows while patient records remain dedicated to direct care. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of conducting a Root Cause Analysis after an adverse event?

options.A: To update the hospital website with public safety performance data
options.B: To find the specific staff member responsible for disciplinary action
options.C: To identify underlying systemic flaws that allowed the event to occur
options.D: To satisfy insurance companies so financial claims can be processed

explanation: Root Cause Analysis looks beyond individual actions to examine structural workflows, environment, and equipment issues. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which question best reflects the core philosophy of a Root Cause Analysis framework?

options.A: What systemic conditions allowed this workflow failure to happen?
options.B: How can we penalize negligence without causing a staff shortage?
options.C: Which nurse was working the night shift when this occurred?
options.D: Why did this particular employee fail to follow standard rules?

explanation: The framework shifts focus from individual culpability to environmental and procedural weaknesses in the care delivery system. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the most appropriate approach when disclosing an adverse event to a patient's family?

options.A: Delay all communication until legal representation is present
options.B: Minimize the impact of the error to prevent emotional distress
options.C: Direct the family exclusively to hospital administrative staff
options.D: Provide an honest, empathetic explanation without defensive excuses

explanation: Open, empathetic disclosure respects the patient and family while fostering trust and institutional accountability. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why is timely disclosure of medical errors beneficial for both patients and healthcare institutions?

options.A: It automatically waives all hospital liability in court proceedings
options.B: It prevents regulatory bodies from launching any future investigations
options.C: It fosters trust, supports emotional healing, and reduces litigation risk
options.D: It shifts full responsibility away from clinical staff to management

explanation: Transparent communication reassures patients and families, which frequently mitigates anger and decreases the likelihood of hostile legal action. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is the core purpose of maintaining a Just Culture in healthcare institutions?

options.A: Ensuring that every medical error results in immediate suspension
options.B: Balancing personal accountability with system-level improvements
options.C: Eliminating all nursing reporting responsibilities from the ward
options.D: Protecting senior management from legal liability during audits

explanation: Just culture creates a safe space where reporting is encouraged while distinguishing between honest mistakes and reckless behavior. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h6)

question: Under a Just Culture model, how should an administrator respond to a nurse who commits an honest, inadvertent slip caused by severe shift fatigue?

options.A: Ignore the incident since no permanent patient harm occurred
options.B: Report the nurse to the national licensing board for criminal negligence
options.C: Instantly terminate employment to set an example for other staff
options.D: Focus on redesigning shift schedules and providing supportive coaching

explanation: Unintentional human errors driven by system factors like fatigue require structural changes and coaching rather than punitive discipline. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h6)

question: What represents the final essential phase of managing an adverse event in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Issuing formal disciplinary warnings to all involved personnel
options.B: Filing the investigation papers away in a secure archive cabinet
options.C: Publicly reprimanding the clinical unit in regional newspapers
options.D: Implementing and monitoring corrective system improvements

explanation: The investigative process is only complete when sustainable changes are put in place and evaluated for effectiveness. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)

question: After identifying that a medication error was caused by look-alike packaging, what is the best corrective action to implement?

options.A: Instruct all nurses to read medication labels more carefully during shifts
options.B: Redesign storage bins and enforce distinct labeling protocols for both drugs
options.C: Punish the nurse who administered the incorrect medication vial
options.D: Ban the use of both medications across every department in the hospital

explanation: Modifying the physical storage environment and workflow addresses the root vulnerability rather than relying solely on human vigilance. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)
